questions.question: What does the voltage of a battery measure in an electric circuit?
options: The total number of electrons present in the wires
The speed at which individual electrons travel
The strength with which the battery can 'push' current around the circuit
The resistance of the wires connecting the components

questions.question: If a series circuit has a 9V battery and two bulbs, what is the relationship between the voltages of the bulbs and the battery?
options: The voltage across each bulb is always 9V regardless of the other bulb.
The sum of the voltages across the two bulbs equals the 9V of the battery.
The voltage across each bulb is always 0V because they cancel each other out.
The difference between the voltages of the two bulbs must equal 9V.

questions.question: Three 1.5V cells are connected together in series to make a single battery. What is the total voltage of this battery?
In which direction does a battery push electric charge (electrons) in a complete circuit?
options: In both directions at the same time, alternating back and forth.
One way round the complete circuit.
Inward towards the center of each component.
Randomly back and forth depending on temperature.

questions.question: What happens to the electrons in a circuit at the moment the switch is turned on?
options: Electrons closest to the battery start moving first, followed by others a few seconds later.
Electrons everywhere in the circuit start moving at the same time.
Only the electrons inside the battery move, while those in the wires stay still.
Electrons move one by one in a chain reaction starting from the negative terminal.

questions.question: How fast do individual electrons typically move through a wire in a circuit?
options: At the speed of light, which is millions of meters per second.
At a very slow speed of just a few millimetres each second.
At approximately the speed of sound.
They do not actually move; they only vibrate in a fixed spot.

questions.question: Why can current not flow through a faulty filament bulb?
options: The glass bulb has become completely opaque to electrons.
The metal base of the bulb has lost its magnetic charge.
The filament inside the bulb is broken, leaving a gap.
The bulb's resistance has dropped to zero, stopping the flow.

questions.question: How can you make a series circuit function if it contains one faulty component that is blocking the current?
options: By adding a second battery in the opposite direction.
By using a wire to bypass the faulty component.
By placing a plastic barrier between the wires and the component.
By removing all other working components from the loop.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a series circuit?
options: An electric circuit with multiple branching pathways for the current.
A circuit that can only function when connected to an alternating current generator.
An electric circuit with one complete loop from one end of a battery to the other end.
A circuit where components are arranged in parallel rows.

questions.question: What effect does a properly connected ammeter have on the current in the circuit it is measuring?
options: It significantly reduces the current to prevent damage to the circuit.
It doubles the current by boosting the battery's push.
It measures the current flowing through it without affecting the current in the circuit.
It stops the current completely while taking a reading.

questions.question: Which statement is true about the electric current in a series circuit?
options: The current is strongest near the positive terminal of the battery.
The current is the same everywhere in the circuit.
The current decreases after passing through each component.
The current is strongest near the negative terminal of the battery.

questions.question: What happens to the current in a series circuit when you add another bulb to it?
options: The current decreases only on the side of the battery after the new bulb.
The current increases only on the side of the battery before the new bulb.
The current changes everywhere, on both sides of the component.
The current remains completely unchanged everywhere in the circuit.

questions.question: How must a voltmeter be connected to measure the voltage across a component in a circuit?
options: In series, as part of the main single loop of the circuit.
Across the terminals of the component.
By replacing the component completely with the voltmeter.
Connected to only one terminal of the battery without touching the component.

questions.question: What happens when two objects with opposite electric charges are brought near each other?
options: They repel each other.
They attract each other.
They exert no force on each other.
They neutralize each other instantly without any force.

questions.question: Why are metals difficult to charge by rubbing?
options: Because they do not contain any electrons or electric charges.
Because electric charge flows through them, preventing charge from building up.
Because rubbing a metal destroys its internal positive charges.
Because they are insulators and do not allow charges to move at all.
